bullets.text: CR 90.3, well inside goals and expectations; net income rose 23% YOY to $363M; commercial auto profitability remained in order; strong first quarter started 2011 with many more positives than not.

Introduced Snapshot discount at the national level; added a multi-product quoting interface so buying auto or special lines combined with Progressive Home Advantage feels more like one transaction rather than two.

Integrated Snapshot marketing launched across traditional, PR, digital, and social formats; added new Flo commercials and debuted 'the Messenger' advertising campaign to impressive early acceptance, expanding perspectives on offerings.
NPW rose ~3% to $3.9B, nearing the $4B milestone; motorcycle units remained solid, but average written premium per cycle declined, with contributing factors including generally older bikes on roads.

Agency auto policy count reclaimed its all-time high, exceeding the April 2006 record; company expects soon to exceed 12M Personal Lines policyholders; nearly 1M households hold multiple Progressive products.

Profitability had a fair share of favorable prior-period reserve development, mostly from 2010; reserve adjustments represent a real opportunity cost in pricing accuracy, with their inevitability managed through frequent reserve analysis.

Rapid state-level rate revisions ensure best knowledge is reflected in consumer street pricing; Snapshot introduces driving-behavior rating variables—when, how much, and how defensively consumers drive—with data relevance being the most compelling point of acceptance.
Both personal auto channels grew, although each reflected slowing consumer activity; Agency written premium rose <2% (auto policies +4%); Direct written premium grew 7% (auto policies +10%).

Commercial auto maintained pricing discipline and orderly profitability; potentially available customers returned in lower volume than hoped and faced very competitive prices, notably in light local, with competitiveness being continuously assessed.

Continued rollout of 'Household View' to customer service representatives, treating households rather than policies as the entity of interest; company directed attention fully toward growth to seek immunity from shopping declines.
